pages.title: Control Center
pages.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE complete high-fidelity desktop web-app screenshot for a new page in ThermaVoltFlow. Image 1 is a STYLE AND COMPONENT REFERENCE, not content to duplicate. Match its dark charcoal background, subtle outlined panels, soft green selected states, clean white sans-serif typography, restrained corner radii, spacing, and fixed narrow left sidebar. Full-screen flat interface, wide 16:10 aspect ratio, readable large text, no browser/device frame or watermark. No presentation captions outside the interface.
Sidebar exact brand: "ThermaVoltFlow". Links in this exact order: "Dashboard", "Control Center", "Smart Scheduler", "Analytics". Highlight only the requested page. Small "DEMO DATA" badge by the page title. All readings are illustrative. Buildable professional product UI with a clear hierarchy and enough breathing room.
Product: three INDEPENDENT systems, Home electricity, Water heating, EV charging. Home and EV each have separate solar-electric panels. Water uses a SOLAR THERMAL HEATER: horizontal silver cylinder above a tilted bank of dark blue cylindrical collector tubes on a triangular stand, matching the reference. Never show photovoltaic panels powering a vertical tank for the water system. Only the home and EV solar installations generate exportable electricity. Thermal heat is separate from electric power accounting.
When showing device illustrations, use simplified smooth matte 3D forms exactly like the reference, no plants or detailed scenery: small house with rooftop PV, horizontal-tank tube water heater, and rounded car with charge post under its own solar canopy.
All three systems have independent choices "Solar", "Grid", "Off", "Schedule". Water grid mode means electric backup heating. Export surplus electricity is an explicit user opt-in and currently OFF. Do not imply thermal heat can be exported to the electrical grid. Use green for solar electricity, amber for grid electricity, warm orange for thermal data, and subdued gray for Off.
Keep text concise and legible. Do not invent extra product sections, batteries, logos or decorative sci-fi visuals. No need to repeat the dashboard's giant central scene; design the requested page for its purpose.
PAGE: "Control Center". Subtitle "Manage each system independently". Highlight Control Center in the sidebar.
Header right: green connection indicator "All systems online" and a restrained red outlined "Turn all off" button.
Below header: slim summary strip with "Solar electricity 5.8 kW", "Grid import 0.0 kW", and "3 systems online".
The dominant content is THREE equal-width tall control panels side by side, each with a compact simplified 3D illustration at the top and substantial usable controls below.
HOME panel: "Home electricity", green badge "Solar active"; large "2.6 kW" current load. Four-way segmented source selector "Solar | Grid | Off | Schedule", Solar selected. "Supply enabled" toggle ON. Compact sparkline titled "Load · last hour". A quiet "Edit schedule" link.
WATER panel: "Water heating", green badge "Solar thermal"; correct simple horizontal-tank evacuated-tube heater illustration; large "54°C" current water temperature. Four-way selector Solar selected. "Target temperature 55°C" with slider. "Electric backup relay" toggle OFF. Small explanatory line "Off disables powered heating". A tiny temperature history sparkline, clearly degrees Celsius, not electrical kW.
EV panel: "EV charging", green badge "Charging"; car, charger and own PV canopy illustration; large "3.2 kW", "Battery 68%" and a simple charge bar. Four-way selector Solar selected. "Charge limit 80%" slider. A prominent but calm red outlined "Stop charging" button. This acts as the requested dedicated EV stop control.
Bottom row split into two clearly aligned panels. LEFT: "Grid export", "Export surplus electricity" with toggle OFF and compact "Solar electricity only · User opt-in", numeric "Export 0.0 kW". RIGHT: "Recent activity", three short time-stamped entries: "12:05 Home switched to solar", "12:02 EV charging started", "11:58 Electric backup turned off".
Keep full controls visible without cropping. The page should look like a realistic sibling of the reference dashboard, richly detailed in interface design but with simple 3D objects.
